Course Contents: 
Unit-1: Need to study Biology-  
Life Science Studies Significance – Bio Inspired Inventions – Role of Biology 
in Next Generation Technology Development – Cell Structure – Cell Potential – 
Action Potential – ECG and other common signals – Sodium 
 
08 Hrs 
Unit -2: Cell Biology- 
Water, Biomolecules, Enzymes, Introduction to metabolism, Cell structure, Cell 
cycle Culture growth, Mendelian genetics 
08 Hrs 

Unit - 3: Molecular Biology- 
Chromatin, DNA structure, replication, transcription and translation 
08 Hrs 
Unit-4: Potassium channels- 
Neuron function – Central Nervous Systems – Discussion Topics: Evolution of 
Artificial Neural Networks, Machine Learning techniques. 
08 Hrs 
Unit-5: Sensing Techniques- 
Understanding of Sense organs working – Sensing mechanisms – Sensor 
Development issues – Discussion Topics: Digital Camera – Eye Comparison, 
electronic nose, electronic tongue, electronic skin. 
08 Hrs

Artificial Organ Development: Kidney, Liver, Pancreas, heart valves – Design 
Challenges and Technological Developments 
               08 Hrs

Course Contents:  
Unit 1:-Introduction to Biomolecules 
Overview of biomolecules: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Lipids, Nucleic acids.  Importance of 
biomolecules in biological systems and the foundations of chemistry of biomolecules  
 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 2:- Proteins:  
Classification, Structure and properties of amino acids, stereochemistry of amino acids , 
absorption spectra, Structure and composition of protein, metabolic disorders associated 
with protein. 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 3:- Carbohydrates: 
Classification and chemical properties of carbohydrates- monosaccharides, disaccharides, 
oligo and polysaccharides, Glycoconjugates (proteoglycans, glycoprotein, glycolipids) 
Metabolism of carbohydrates and associated metabolic disorders.  
6 Hrs. 
Unit 4:--- Lipids: 
Classification and chemical properties of lipids, Function of lipids (simple- storage and 
functional-membrane lipids) Metabolism of lipids, Metabolism Disorders. 
8 Hrs. 

Unit 5:- Nucleic acids: 
Classification, Structure, function, Central dogma, Metabolic disorders 
8Hrs. 
Unit 6:--- Biochemical Techniques: 
Introduction to common techniques used to study the biomolecules such as electrophoresis, 
SDS PAGE, Edman degradation, Sanger sequencing method, Next generation sequencing,  
X-ray crystallography, etc  
7 Hrs.
